correctness.rationale: The opening Finding admits s∈(0,1] and says that b=1 always has a gain with a nonzero nilpotent return Jacobian. At the included orthogonal endpoint u=e₁, v=e₂, b=1, the return Jacobian is diag(1−a,0); it is nilpotent only at a=1, when it is zero. Exact annihilation then takes just two steps in the quadratic model. The detailed theorem restricts its nonzero and four-step assertion to 0<s<1, and that qualified theorem is correct. Independently, T=(I−bvvᵀ)(I−auuᵀ) has trace 2−a−b+ab(1−s) and determinant (1−a)(1−b); the three quadratic Schur inequalities reduce to the two displayed inequalities and abs>0. If the determinant exceeds one then some modulus exceeds one, and a negative characteristic-polynomial value at −1 forces a real root below −1. For b=1 the spectrum is {0,1−as}; at a=1/s with s<1 the return is nonzero of rank one and squares to zero, while invertibility of the first phase precludes uniform three-step annihilation. At a nonlinear stationary point the chain rule gives the same return derivative and a Taylor bound gives local quadratic attraction of G², not exact nonlinear annihilation. Thus the frozen opening assertion, not the restricted derivation, is refuted.

value.rationale: The model is natural, but the surviving facts are routine deductions without a substantive new boundary phenomenon beyond the standard product calculation. The unrestricted 2×2 region is the textbook second-order Jury test applied directly to trace and determinant. With b=1, the return lands on the line v⊥; for a unit w on that line it acts by the scalar 1−a(uᵀw)²=1−as. Therefore placing this scalar at zero both forces the two-return cancellation and makes the large gain 1/s transparent; its divergence as the angle closes needs no additional result. The claimed nonlinear effect is then exactly the universal chain-rule/Taylor consequence of a square-zero derivative, with no new nonlinear coefficient, boundary behavior, or robustness quantified. Correcting the orthogonal sentence would leave only these standard deductions, so no valuable repair was supplied.
residual_risks: This does not judge the value of the broader alternating-projection or modified-gradient problems; it concerns only the stated two-dimensional calculation and automatic local lift.
